ch19.d.N: Number of gas molecules (disks) in the box
ch19.d.T: Temperature of the gas; sets the mean molecular kinetic energy $kT$ (2D)
ch19.d.L: Side length $L$ of the square box
ch19.d.init: Speed distribution of the molecules at the start
ch19.d.arrows: Velocity $\vec v$ arrow on every molecule
ch19.goal.sum: Pressure = time average of the impulses $2mv_x$ that many molecules deliver to the wall
ch19.goal.ideal: Compare the measured pressure with the ideal-gas prediction $pA = NkT$ (2D)
ch19.obs.J: Impulse $J$ delivered to the right wall: rises in steps, one per bounce; its mean slope is the mean force on the wall (dashed: ideal gas)
ch19.obs.fluct: The 10 ps moving average of the pressure fluctuates strongly; the average since the start, $J/(Lt)$, converges to the dashed line $NkT/A$
ch19.obs.N: Larger $N$: the pressure grows in proportion to $N$ and the relative fluctuations shrink
ch19.obs.T: Doubling the temperature: molecules move faster and hit more often, so the pressure doubles
ch19.obs.hist: Histogram below: how many molecules are in each speed bin right now (live). Dashed: the expected count $N f(v)\,\Delta v$ from the 2D Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution. Even from one common speed, collisions reshape the bars towards the dashed curve; with small $N$ the bars fluctuate strongly. A bar taller than the axis shows its count on top
ch19.assume.2d: 2D gas: pressure = force per unit wall length (mN/m = pN/nm), area $A = L^2$
ch19.assume.3d: Link to the textbook's 3D formula: 2D $pA = \tfrac12 Nm\overline{v^2} = NkT$ (mean kinetic energy per molecule $\tfrac12 m\overline{v^2} = kT$) ↔ 3D $pV = \tfrac13 Nm\overline{v^2} = NkT$ (mean kinetic energy $\tfrac32 kT$). In both, $\overline{v_x^2} = kT/m$
ch19.assume.disk: Hard disks the size of helium atoms (diameter 0.26 nm, mass $6.65\times10^{-27}$ kg), perfectly elastic collisions, smooth walls. Where the disks would cover more than 1.5 % of the box, their diameter shrinks to keep 1.5 % (ideal gas: molecule size negligible; 0.066 nm at $N = 1000$, $L = 15$ nm)
ch19.assume.dense: The disks' size makes the measured pressure slightly higher than $NkT/A$: the area the disks block for each other, $2\varphi$ (area fraction $\varphi \le 1.5$ %), plus a wall layer $\sigma/L$ (a disk centre stops one radius from the wall, so the width it moves in is $L - \sigma$; $\sigma/L \le 1.7$ %). Together $2\varphi + \sigma/L$: about 4 % at the defaults, within about 5 % at every setting
ch19.assume.relax: Collision rate: at the defaults a molecule collides about 36 times in 200 ps. At $N = 20$, $L = 30$ nm, 100 K only about twice, so the run ends before the speed distribution has fully reached the Maxwell-Boltzmann form
ch19.assume.win: During the first 10 ps both pressure plots divide the impulse so far by 10 ps, so they start from 0
